title: Eviction-Priming Orchestrator for Zero-downtime VPC Runtime Upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement an orchestration component (Eviction-Priming Orchestrator) that coordinates zero-downtime runtime upgrades for Private/VPC data planes. The orchestrator must integrate with our Terraform/IaC pipelines, runtime health probes, and tenant-aware KV/cache priming to avoid cold-cache/noisy-police failures during switchover. Problem: upgrades today occasionally cause large latency spikes and client errors for tenants when priming (KV/cache) or in-flight sessions are not reconciled. The goal is safe phased switchover with automatic gating and deterministic rollback behavior.
background: We have frequent private deployment upgrades across heterogeneous customer slices. Existing rollouts sometimes evict primed KV caches and cause tenant-visible errors during the first traffic after switchover. This ticket builds a controller that understands eviction/priming, coordinates drain+prime phases, and ties into Terraform-driven maintenance windows. It must operate without adding single points of failure and provide clear observability and runbook hooks for on-call.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator coordinates a staged upgrade across a tenant slice without increasing p50 latency by >10% and without increasing 5xx errors for primed tenants. 2) Health gating prevents promotion if synthetic priming probes fail for >=2 consecutive checks. 3) Rollback completes within configured window (default 10 minutes) and restores previous runtime image and connections without double-serving or dropped KV state. 4) Terraform module exposes hooks for maintenance windows, drain timeouts, and preflight checks. 5) Automated e2e test in CI reproduces a simulated cache eviction and validates recovery. 6) Docs and a step-by-step runbook are added to the private-upgrades space.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight control loop deployed as part of the private control plane. Phases: PRECHECK -> DRAIN -> PRIME -> SCHEDULE -> SWITCHOVER -> VALIDATE -> FINALIZE. Precheck runs Terraform plan validations and inventory snapshot. DRAIN uses grace period + connection tracker to avoid breaking in-flight streams. PRIME runs tenant-specific synthetic requests to warm KV caches and warm model context where applicable. SCHEDULE staggers switchover across slots to maintain capacity. VALIDATE uses synthetic probes and live telemetry to verify SLOs. FINALIZE commits state in the orchestration ledger.
terraform_integration: - Provide a module private_upgrade_orchestrator that wires maintenance window, IAM roles, and webhook endpoints for the orchestrator. - Preflight terraform plan hook to fail fast on unsafe networking/IAM changes. - Use tags on compute resources to map tenant slices for targeted upgrades. - Expose variables: drain_timeout, prime_timeout, slot_size, canary_percentage, fallback_policy.
health_checks: - Synthetic priming probes per-tenant with configurable assertion sets (tokens, KV hit rate, request latency). - Distributed quorum of health agents to avoid noisy single-point failures. - Liveness + readiness for orchestrator components. - Telemetry hooks for token-level cost and latency breakdowns to identify priming regressions.
rollback_playbook: 1) Abort ongoing switchovers via orchestrator API and set cluster to rollback mode. 2) Trigger Terraform apply to re-deploy previous runtime image (image tag pinned in rollout ledger). 3) Rewind orchestration ledger to pre-upgrade snapshot and reattach old slot endpoints. 4) Drain any partially upgraded pods to avoid split-brain. 5) Re-run PRIME phase against the restored runtime to reconcile KV caches. 6) Run smoke tests across a sample of tenants and monitor 5xx/latency for 15 minutes. 7) If stable, mark rollback complete and schedule postmortem. Notes: rollback must be automatable but require on-call ack for cross-tenant operations with high customer impact.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for control loop transitions. - Integration tests that run orchestrator against a local-kind VPC mimic with synthetic probes. - CI e2e that performs a canary upgrade and forces a priming failure to validate gating + rollback. - Chaos test: random eviction of KV nodes during PRIME/DRAIN phases to ensure graceful recovery. - Load test with realistic sequence length distributions to validate kernel selection doesn't regress during switchover.
telemetry_and_alerting: - Dashboards: per-slot rollout progress, priming success rate, drain lag, 5xx count, p50/p95 latency per-tenant. - Alerts: HealthGateFailure (>=2 consecutive probe failures), DrainStuck (drain exceeds configured timeout), RollbackTriggered, CanaryRegressions. - Tracing: correlation id propagated through switch to identify requests spanning switchover.
security_considerations: - Orchestrator webhooks must use mTLS and IAM-scoped service accounts. - Terraform module must avoid exposing secrets; use KMS/HSM references. - Audit logs emitted for every upgrade/rollback action for compliance. - Security review required to ensure no escalation path for operators to access tenant data.
